Role Overview 
 We are seeking an experienced Senior Frontend Engineer to contribute to the modernization and performance optimization of a large-scale financial services platform. The role involves working within established engineering teams to enhance the responsiveness, stability, scalability and maintainability of complex, data-intensive applications used in demanding financial workflows.
 The ideal candidate will combine strong hands-on frontend development expertise with experience diagnosing and resolving performance challenges in real-time or high-concurrency applications.
 Key Responsibilities 
Develop, maintain and optimize frontend applications using React and/or Angular with TypeScript and JavaScript.
Investigate and resolve application responsiveness, rendering performance and resource utilization issues.
Optimize complex, data-intensive user interfaces, including applications processing frequently updated or real-time information.
Contribute to frontend architecture, component design, maintainability and application scalability.
Identify performance bottlenecks using profiling, monitoring and diagnostic tools.
Integrate frontend applications with REST APIs and backend services.
Develop automated tests and contribute to CI/CD engineering practices.
Collaborate with backend, platform, architecture and reliability engineering teams to resolve cross-layer performance issues.
Participate in code reviews, technical discussions and continuous engineering improvements.
Ensure solutions comply with established security, accessibility and engineering standards.
 Mandatory Technical Skills 
Strong hands-on experience with JavaScript, TypeScript and React and/or Angular.
Solid understanding of frontend architecture, component-based development and modern web application design.
Practical experience optimizing frontend performance, including rendering efficiency, memory utilization and application responsiveness.
Experience developing large-scale, data-intensive or real-time applications.
Strong understanding of asynchronous programming, API integration and client-side state management.
Experience with automated testing, debugging, performance profiling and CI/CD practices.
Working knowledge of cloud-hosted applications and distributed application architectures.
 Domain Experience 
Strong preference for experience developing trading platforms, market-data applications or other financial markets systems.
Candidates with demonstrable experience building high-concurrency, performance-sensitive applications in banking, payments or similarly demanding environments may also be considered.
 Preferred Skills 
Experience with real-time data delivery mechanisms such as WebSockets or streaming APIs.
Familiarity with Node.js and full-stack development.
Experience with AWS or Azure.
Knowledge of observability, application monitoring and performance testing.
Experience optimizing applications handling high-frequency data updates.
 About Us: 
 Ascendion is a global, leading provider of AI-first software engineering services, delivering transformative solutions across North America, APAC, and Europe. We are headquartered in New Jersey. We combine technology and talent to deliver tech debt relief, improve engineering productivity solutions, and accelerate time to value, driving our clients’ digital journeys with efficiency and velocity. Guided by our “Engineering to the power of AI” [EngineeringAI] methodology, we integrate AI into software engineering, enterprise operations, and talent orchestration, to address critical challenges of trust, speed, and capital. For more information, please go to www.ascendion.com
 With Ascendion (www.ascendion.com), you:
Will get to work on numerous challenging and exciting projects on our various offerings including Salesforce, AI/Data Science, Generative AI/ML, Automation, Cloud Enterprise and Product/Platform Engineering.
At Ascendion you have high chances of project extension or redeployment to other clients.
Additionally, you can also share CV of anyone you know. We have a referral policy in place.
